sources.name: Yarotsky, Perturbations of ground states in weakly interacting quantum spin systems
sources.usedFor: a weak bounded finite-range perturbation of a noninteracting lattice with nondegenerate uniformly gapped local ground states retains a unique gapped ground state for sufficiently small local strength

sources.name: Yarotsky, Quasi-particles in weak perturbations of non-interacting quantum lattice systems
sources.usedFor: the same noninteracting gapped setting and perturbative quasiparticle continuation

sources.name: Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis, Topological quantum order: stability under local perturbations
sources.usedFor: comparison boundary only; its commuting-projector and topological-order hypotheses are not established for the rotor strip

theoremLevelConclusion.statement: For fixed N=8 there exists a nonzero local perturbation-strength threshold, independent of the number of periodic bulk cells, below which the unique bulk ground state and a positive spectral gap persist.

nonApplications: The finite-device global-norm inequality is not a thermodynamic local-perturbation bound.
The Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis commuting-projector TQO theorem is not invoked because LTQO and a commuting-projector parent were not established.
The fixed-cutoff theorem does not justify interchanging weak-coupling, thermodynamic and N-to-infinity limits.
A stable trivial product bulk does not by itself determine the Leech K-matrix or chiral boundary CFT.

observables: ground-state fidelity susceptibility per bulk cell
open-strip edge tower measured separately after the periodic bulk scan
experimentalRadiusProtocol.pass: at least one nonzero contiguous strength interval has a positive thermodynamic gap lower confidence bound stable across Y and unchanged within tolerance from N=8 to N=16
experimentalRadiusProtocol.fail: all nonzero strengths extrapolate to gap closure, the apparent radius shrinks to zero with Y or N, or the edge record changes before the bulk criterion is met

established: a source-backed thermodynamic existence bridge for weak local perturbations at fixed finite rotor cutoff, plus an explicit protocol for measuring the otherwise unknown stability radius
boundary: No numerical stability threshold is claimed. Uniform control as N tends to infinity, chiral-edge stability, the Leech response and the Monster extension remain open.
